newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end slightly higher.

text.p: Swiss shares ended a listless and rangebound session slightly higher after posting moderate gains early in the session on the back of Wall Street's strength on Friday.

"The fundamentals continue to look good, but I think the SMI will hover around 3,800 points until the end of the week", one dealer said. He said Friday's expiry on options and futures may lead to some price volatility in blue-chip shares.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was up 8.5 points, or 0.22 percent, to 3,813.7 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index added 5.24 points, or 0.22 percent, to 2,440.88.
Buy orders from British investors buoyed Roche certificates, which rose 70 francs to 9,655. Some brokers saw a price target of 10,000 francs for the stock, one dealer said.
Roche said in a statement after the bourse close it would release its group sales figures for the first nine months on October 15.

Rumours about an imminent press conference by Sulzer about a restructuring at the company's Rueti unit boosted the shares, a dealer said. Sulzer said later it would give detailed figures in connection with the restructuring at Rueti on Thursday. The stocks jumped 16 francs to 753.
Among banks, UBS bearer shares rose two francs to 1,259. One dealer cited recurring rumours the bank may announce a restructuring sooner or later.

SBC and CS Holding lost 0.7 and 0.6 percent, respectively. Insurer Zurich saw good volumes, adding two francs to 359. One dealer said the stock was approaching the critical level of 360 francs, which has proved to be a strong resistance in the past.
Insurer Winterthur rose nine francs to 785. Winterthur confirmed China had agreed in principle to make it the first European insurer to get a domestic licence.
